paragraphs: R. Yoshiyah “of his generation”: Avodah Zarah, R. Yishmael, 51, in R. Yochanan's and R. Elazar's time, excluding R. Yoshiyah the Elder. Arukh, final entry Dor, explains “of his generation” as his contemporary, implying there was an elder there. End of quotation. Menachot 71a: R. Elazar said, “Do not sit on your feet until you explain it to me.” Rashi explains that he was of his generation and age, excluding R. Yoshiyah the Great, a tanna. Kiddushin 36b: R. Elazar said to R. Yoshiyah of his generation. Rashi explains that he was an amora of his own generation and infers that R. Yoshiyah, R. Yonatan's disputant, was still alive then, and the qualification excludes R. Yoshiyah the Elder. Sotah, beginning of chapter 3, 19a: Rashi explains that he was an amora in R. Elazar ben Pedat's generation, excluding R. Yoshiyah the tanna, R. Yonatan's disputant, who was old: it would not be respectful to tell him, “Do not sit on your feet until you explain it to me.” He studied with R. Matya ben Cheresh, then turned to worldly occupation; see Shocher Tov there. R. Yoshiyah and R. Abba bar Zavda went out for a fast: Jerusalem Taanit, beginning of chapter 2. R. Avdimi, grandson through a daughter of R. Tavi, in his name. R. Aivu, in his name. R. Acha son of R. Yoshiyah. R. Chaga, in his name. R. Chaggai questioned him: Jerusalem Talmud, Ben Sorer. R. Tavi, in his name. R. Tuvyah bar Mattana said: R. Yoshiyah. R. Yonatan ben Chali, in his name. R. Yaakov bar Acha, in his name. R. Yitzchak bar Redifa questioned him. Rav Kahana. Rav Menashya bar Azza questioned him. He transmitted in Rav’s name—Sukkah 2b. He said to R. Shimon bar Chiyya. R. Tanchum bar Ilai.
